column1: # Where every agent skill comes from. One row per skill, TSV, '# ' comments.
#   id <TAB> kind <TAB> spec <TAB> why
# kind:
#   repo    link <checkout>/skills/<id> into ~/.agents/skills.
#           spec = GitHub repository that owns the skill. Linked from a checkout
#           when one exists (so it updates with `git pull`), otherwise fetched
#           with `npx skills add <repo> --skill <id> -g`. The CLI does not
#           discover every layout, so a clone is the reliable path.
#   dagr    owned by the herdr-dagr plugin. Extracted with `dagr --skill` into
#           that plugin's own skills/ directory (next to its examples/), then
#           linked. spec = herdr plugin id that provides the dagr binary.
#   bundle  no installable home exists, so this repo is the source of truth.
#           spec = path in this repo. This is debt: the `why` says what would
#           let it be deleted, and scripts/skills-sync.sh reports the count.
# All five live in one repository, each in its own top-level directory with its
# own pyproject/Makefile. They are NOT in skills/ and `npx skills add` does not
# find them (verified: "No valid skills found"), so the only reliable install is
# a checkout, linked per directory.
# A checkout at <root>/mycord takes precedence over the skills under
# ~/.agents/skills, because the repo carries .env.example and the current text
# while the copies there have drifted. If you already keep the skills there as
# hand-copies, see docs/mycord.md for the one-time cleanup.
yellowstone
column4: This repo's own install/configure/upgrade guide; home is this repo by definition.

column1: hotshot
column4: Apothic-AI/one-shot-genius exists but is empty (0 bytes, no commits), so `npx skills add` cannot fetch it yet. Becomes kind=repo once the skill is pushed.

column1: herdr
column4: Fork of the skill `herdr --skill` ships: ~56 delta lines, mostly target-verification-before-delegation, which this orchestration setup depends on. Rebase onto the shipped file when herdr changes and send the delta upstream; becomes kind=shipped when herdr takes it.

column1: dagr-producer
column4: Owned by the herdr-dagr plugin pinned in herdr/plugins.toml. Never bundle: `dagr --skill` is byte-identical to the plugin's own copy, so a bundled copy is a silent fork of a file the plugin already owns.

column1: unblock
column4: Owned by our fork, which ships skills/unblock/SKILL.md. The fork's copy is newer than any bundled copy (it documents queue-page sign-in), so bundling would freeze agents on a stale skill.

column1: mycord-discord-skill
column4: The comms space's Discord surface (discord.py-self REPL). User-account automation: violates Discord's ToS and can get the account banned - never initiate unprompted.

column1: mycord-telegram-skill
column4: The comms space's Telegram surface (Telethon REPL). Supports real user accounts; Telegram permits third-party clients.

column1: mycord-irc-skill
column4: The comms space's IRC surface (pydle REPL), TLS by default.

column1: mycord-email-skill
column4: The comms space's email surface: Himalaya CLI with a per-account wrapper config.

column1: google-voice-skill
column4: The comms space's SMS/voice surface (unofficial gvoice TS client). Reading works; sending SMS needs a captured exchange.
